title: Slate tile packer: adaptive tile-based batch formation with KV-tiling and GPU budget enforcement for streaming chat
creator: Anita Chowdhury
description: Problem: For streaming chat completions we need a batch formation strategy that minimizes tail latency while maximizing GPU utilization and respecting a strict per-GPU memory budget. Existing continuous-batching approaches either over-consolidate multi-turn sessions (increasing KV cache pressure) or under-bundle short-turn traffic (wasting kernel throughput). This ticket proposes a new 'slate tile packer' heuristic that treats incoming streaming requests as tiles placed into a bounded slate per worker, with explicit KV-tiling and GPU memory budgeting to avoid OOMs and excessive KV thrashing.
proposal_notes:
Design overview:
- Slate abstraction: each worker maintains a small number (N) of slates. A slate is a soft timebox/packet that holds a set of tiles (requests) to be assembled into a single GPU invocation.
- Tile: compact descriptor for a request containing: request_id, session_id hash, turn_length_estimate, current_kv_size_estimate, priority, deadline (deadline = now + latency_SLO_remaining).
- KV-tiling: instead of assuming whole-session KV per-tile, store and track KV slices: hot KV prefix (recent tokens within X turns) is pinned, cold KV pages are referenced via indices and loaded on-demand into a per-slate working set. This reduces per-slate committed KV footprint.
- GPU budget enforcement: each slate computes an estimated GPU working set = sum(tile_model_context + tile_kv_working_set) + kernel_scratch. Slate creation is denied if worker.available_gpu_budget < estimated_working_set_threshold.
- Adaptive packer: tiles are placed into slates by scoring function S = w1*(1 - normalized_deadline_slack) + w2*(priority_score) + w3*(1 - kv_size_norm) + w4*(context_compatibility_score). Context compatibility prefers grouping tiles with overlapping KV pages (to amortize KV loads).
- Timeboxing + progressive flush: slates flush when either (a) timebox expires, (b) estimated GPU efficiency delta if we add another tile falls below epsilon, or (c) a hard deadline tile needs emission.
- Fallbacks: if slate admission is blocked repeatedly, a ticket-level fallback routes requests to lower-cost model variants (shorter context) or to a dedicated micro-worker with higher memory headroom.
- Telemetry & safety: every slate logs estimated_vs_actual_gpu_memory, KV_load_hits, and per-tile latency contribution. Anti-opaqueness: offline analysis can reconstruct how tiles were scored and packed.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Implement slate lifecycle (create/pause/flush) and tile scoring in runtime worker.
2) KV-tiling metadata flows from session store; worker can compute per-tile kv_size_estimate without pulling entire KV.
3) Slate enforces an explicit GPU working set budget and refuses admission when threshold exceeded (with a fallback path).
4) E2E integration test: under a synthetic streaming workload (mixed short/long turns), 95th percentile tail latency should not worsen vs baseline and GPU utilization improves by >= 8% for steady-state traffic.
5) No OOM occurrences in a 48-hour soak on canary cluster with congested KV distributions.
6) Dashboard panels for slate metrics added to Console: slate_count, avg_tiles_per_slate, kv_load_hit_rate, slate_memory_estimation_error.
success_metrics:
- 95p tail latency for streaming completions: <= baseline + 5ms
- GPU utilization: +8% steady-state
- KV load hit rate: +5% (more shared pages per slate)
- Slate memory estimation error (abs(avg_estimated - actual)/actual): < 12%
- Fallback rate (requests needing micro-worker or model downgrade): < 2% under normal production load
test_plan:
Unit tests:
- tile scoring correctness (edge cases: large KV, tight deadlines)
- slate admission/denial logic with mocked GPU budget
Integration tests:
- Synthetic mix generator: 60% short (<=16 tokens), 30% medium (17-128), 10% long (>128) streams with session affinity. Run against canary cluster comparing baseline batching algo vs slate tile packer.
- OOM stress test: artificially inflate per-session KV to validate fallback correctness.
Perf benchmarks:
- Run with perf harness (github.com/redwood/bench/run-slates) capturing per-slate telemetry, KV load patterns, GPU memory traces.
Chaos tests:
- Kill a worker mid-slate, ensure requeue behavior and KV consistency.
Acceptance soak:
- 48h on canary under 2x normal QPS with diversified KV hot/cold distributions.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): 10% traffic on dedicated canary pool; collect telemetry and refine scoring weights (w1..w4).
Phase 2 (extended canary): 50% traffic for 72h, enable automatic fallback triggers to block admission if memory estimation repeatedly underestimates.
Phase 3 (gradual): 10% increments every 6 hours to 100% if canary metrics stable.
Rollback: disable packer and revert to current continuous-batching system; all in-flight tiles either flushed or requeued onto baseline.
Docs: update 'Serving runtime batching strategies' doc and add a design note explaining KV-tiling and GPU budget model.
blockers:
- Need session-store API extension to expose per-session KV page indices and recent-hot-window size without full KV fetch (engineering infra task).
- Kernel memory accounting APIs must expose accurate scratch estimates per model and sequence length (research/infra dependency).
- MXNet/CUDA/NCCL driver anomalies reported in PR #976 hanging on partial GPU free calls (investigation required).
